text: Discovery: 361 rows, 110 positives, 6 systems under LOGO CV. Base rates are extremely heterogeneous: Afasevikumab-IL17A 1/62, Bimagrumab-ACVR2B 7/68, Eculizumab-C5 13/72, Spesolimab-IL36R 16/58, Osocimab-FXI 19/43, Tezepelumab-TSLP 54/58. Two of the six folds are near-degenerate: Afasevikumab contributes a single positive (its fold ROC-AUC is one row percentile rank) and Tezepelumab has only 4 negatives. One third of the primary metric is therefore decided by 5 rows, and a single rank swap in either fold moves macro ROC-AUC by about 0.003.

Rule 7 check on the three signals prepare flagged below 0.5 pooled (ABB2 HCDR3 0.498, ABB3 0.342, ESMFold 0.396). This is a Simpson effect, not an inverted direction: per-system raw medians differ by up to 7x (ABB2 HCDR3 median 0.53 angstrom in Bimagrumab vs 3.91 in Eculizumab) and the level offsets are unrelated to the base rate, so pooling mixes between-system offsets into the ranking. Within systems the declared direction holds for the baseline signal (macro LOGO AUC 0.622 vs pooled 0.498). No direction was changed.

Within-system (LOGO) macro oriented AUC per signal: ABB2 HCDR3 0.622 [0.90/0.77/0.71/0.49/0.39/0.47 across the six systems], Fv ABB2 0.609 [0.93/0.91/0.59/0.50/0.39/0.33], ABB3 HCDR3 0.516, ESMFold HCDR3 0.486. Spearman correlation with the baseline signal after within-system ranking: Fv 0.863 (redundant), ABB3 0.138, ESMFold -0.018. So the one informative partner is redundant and the two near-orthogonal partners are at or below chance. ESMFold looks complementary across systems (0.83 in Eculizumab, 0.76 in Spesolimab where ABB2 is 0.71 and 0.39) but is harmful in Bimagrumab (0.26) and Afasevikumab (0.08), so its skill is system-dependent, not stable.

Mechanism checks on the rule language, all on discovery rows. (1) Every signal occupies only 0.3 to 5.2 angstrom of the declared 0..10 range, so the product and additive forms of a pair are rank-equivalent here: spearman 0.9999 with 0.2 percent discordant pairs for HCDR3 x Fv, macro AUC 0.6225 additive vs 0.6244 product. Disclosure: I computed those two macro AUCs, plus 0.5894 additive and 0.5840 product for HCDR3 ABB2 x ABB3 at equal weights, while establishing that equivalence, so the additive evaluations below are confirmatory rather than blind; I will not evaluate the product forms, which are duplicates of the additive ones in rank terms. (2) Fv ABB2 spans 0.14 of the normalized range (sd 0.41) against 1.19 for the HCDR3 signals, so equal additive weights do not mean equal influence. (3) A gate whose adjustment uses only its own gating signal is a monotone reshaping of the baseline and cannot move any rank metric.

Absolute-threshold gates cannot be made system-neutral in this language: the group column is not a legal rule term and the systems sit at different absolute levels. Measured coverage per system, ABB2 HCDR3 > 2.5: 0.97 Eculizumab, 0.48 Afasevikumab, 0.47 Osocimab, 0.17 Tezepelumab, 0.01 Bimagrumab, 0.00 Spesolimab, leaving 2 of 6 folds usable inside the gate; ABB3 > 2.0: 1.00/1.00/0.79/0.65/0.29/0.07. Fv ABB2 never exceeds 1.82 angstrom on discovery, so the conventional 2 angstrom framework-quality gate is empty and Fv > 1.5 sits inside one system. Any gated gain on macro LOGO AUC is thus confounded with which systems the gate selects. Inside ABB2 > 2.5 the local within-system AUCs are ESMFold 0.670 (2 usable folds: 0.82 Eculizumab, 0.52 Osocimab) and ABB2 0.581; that is the regime campaigns/demo already tested, where it gave ROC +0.008 and broke the precision@10 guard. Inside ABB3 > 2.5 (6 systems) ABB2 still leads at 0.599 while ABB3 falls to 0.227 and ESMFold to 0.392, so no second opinion takes over there.

Pre-registered plan: three global-form ideas, each with a stated mechanism. (1) scope consensus, averaging HCDR3 and Fv ABB2 to cut per-candidate measurement noise; (2) predictor consensus, baseline plus a small pre-stated 0.25 weight on ABB3, the most nearly orthogonal antibody-specific second predictor; (3) three-predictor loop ensemble at equal weights, testing noise averaging against signal dilution. Expected effects are small and the diagnostics make a real win unlikely. Disclosure: before this campaign the working tree already held three untracked rule files (rules/scope-consensus.json, rules/scope-conjunction.json, rules/predictor-consensus.json) and a results/research directory from an earlier look at this same dataset, so ideas 1 and 2 are not independent of that earlier look; I am writing fresh rule files under search-1 names rather than reusing those.

formula: score = (1 * n("HCDR3 scRMSD (ABB2)", 0..10, lower_is_better) + 1 * n("Fv scRMSD (ABB2)", 0..10, lower_is_better)) / 2
hypothesis: Cross-scope noise averaging within one predictor. HCDR3 and Fv scRMSD from ABB2 are two readings of the same latent quantity, how self-consistently the design folds, taken at different structural scopes; on discovery they are comparably informative within systems (macro LOGO AUC 0.622 for the loop, 0.609 for the framework) and correlated 0.863 after within-system ranking. If part of each reading is per-candidate prediction noise rather than real design quality, averaging two correlated readings of the same quantity should cancel some of that noise and rank slightly better than either alone, without introducing a new mechanism or a new failure mode. Equal weights follow from the comparable within-system AUCs and were not swept; note that equal weights still give the framework term about a third of the influence, because Fv occupies 0.14 of the declared 0..10 range against 0.44 for the loop. Expected gain is small, at most a few thousandths of macro ROC-AUC, since the two readings are 0.86 correlated and so share most of their noise; a drop in PR-AUC or any precision@K would mean the framework reading is diluting rather than denoising.

text: Idea 1 (s1-scope-mean-abb2) is within-noise: macro ROC-AUC +0.0002 against a paired noise yardstick of 0.0072, no guard broken (PR-AUC -0.0010, precision@20 +0.0167). Per-fold deltas do not point one way: Bimagrumab +0.030, Osocimab +0.007, Afasevikumab 0.000, Spesolimab -0.001, Eculizumab -0.016, Tezepelumab -0.019. Learned: the denoising hypothesis fails as stated. The framework reading moves ranks where it disagrees with the loop reading, but it moves them up in one system and down in two, which is what you expect if the disagreement is noise in both readings rather than noise in one. At 0.86 within-system correlation there was little independent information to average, and the measurement confirms that. Next: switch from the redundant partner to the most nearly orthogonal antibody-specific one, ABB3 HCDR3 (within-system spearman 0.138, macro AUC 0.516), at the small pre-stated weight 0.25 that its narrow margin above chance justifies. This is a different mechanism, cross-predictor agreement rather than cross-scope averaging, and it is the only remaining partner with both above-chance within-system skill and low redundancy.

formula: score = (1 * n("HCDR3 scRMSD (ABB2)", 0..10, lower_is_better) + 0.25 * n("HCDR3 scRMSD (ABB3)", 0..10, lower_is_better)) / 1.25
hypothesis: Cross-predictor agreement on the same loop. ABB3 HCDR3 scRMSD is the most nearly independent partner the dataset offers among signals with above-chance within-system skill: spearman 0.138 against the baseline after within-system ranking, versus 0.863 for Fv, with macro LOGO AUC 0.516. Two separately trained antibody-specific structure predictors agreeing that a designed loop is self-consistent should be harder to satisfy by a single predictor artefact than one predictor agreeing with itself, so the agreement term should add information that idea 1 could not, exactly because it is not redundant. Its within-system margin above chance is 0.016 against the baseline margin of 0.122, so it gets the pre-stated weight 0.25 rather than equal credit; the weight was not swept and no neighbourhood was examined. Counter-hypothesis, which the measurement will discriminate: ABB3 is near chance within systems because its errors are correlated with real design quality in the wrong direction, in which case even a quarter weight should cost a little ROC-AUC. Known in advance from the mechanism check in the journal: the same two signals at equal weight give macro AUC 0.5894, about -0.033 against the baseline, so a quarter weight is expected to land near -0.008, within or just beyond the noise yardstick and in the losing direction.

text: Idea 2 (s2-weak-abb3-consensus) is guard-broken on the primary metric: macro ROC-AUC -0.0194 against a paired noise yardstick of 0.0258, so it cannot be selected whatever else it does. The counter-hypothesis in its pre-written hypothesis is the one that survived: ABB3 is near chance within systems because it carries real error, not averageable noise, and a quarter weight already costs about what a quarter of the equal-weight penalty predicted (-0.008 predicted, -0.019 measured). Per-fold: Bimagrumab -0.103, Eculizumab -0.064, Osocimab -0.026, Tezepelumab -0.019, against Afasevikumab +0.016 and Spesolimab +0.079, and Spesolimab is exactly the system where ABB3 alone beats ABB2 alone (0.638 vs 0.391), so the help and the harm are both system-specific. Worth recording honestly: the top of the ranking improved while the global ordering got worse (precision@10 +0.0167, precision@20 +0.0333, PR-AUC -0.0055). That is a real pattern, but with 110 positives over 6 folds it is also what a 2-row reshuffle at the top looks like, and the broken ROC-AUC guard settles the verdict. Next: the pre-registered three-predictor ensemble at equal weights. Ideas 1 and 2 tested the two extremes of partner redundancy, 0.863 and 0.138; the three-way average is the strongest form of the noise-averaging argument and its prediction is quantitative, so it is the decisive test of that mechanism rather than a repetition.
